body.p: The following remarks are made in response to the Action. In this response, claims 1, 6, 7, 9, and 10 have been amended. Claim 5 has been canceled without prejudice or disclaimer. No claims are newly added. Claims 1-4 and 6-10 are pending. The claim amendments are supported by at least, for example, paragraphs [0043], [0044], [0047], and [0048] of the Specification as filed. There is no new matter.
The drawings are objected to under 37 CFR §1.83(a) for failing to show every feature of the invention specified in the claims. Applicant traverses the objection.

The Action states that the "bevel gears" (claim 7) in combination with "a second axis offset from the first axis" (claim 1 from which claim 7 depends) must be shown or the features canceled." (Action at p. 2.) Support for the feature "a second axis offset from the first axis" is shown in FIG. 2 of the Drawings and at least, for example, paragraphs [0043] and [0044] of the Specification as filed.

Moreover, 37 CFR §1.83(a) states that "conventional features disclosed in the description and the claims, where their detailed illustration is not essential for a proper understanding of their invention, should be illustrated in the drawing." The "bevel gears" are supported by at least, for example, paragraphs [0013] and [0059] of the Specification. Furthermore, a person of ordinary skill in the art (POSITA) would appreciate that the "bevel gears," as recited in claim 7 are a conventional feature related to transmission means for improving the flexibility of the robot. (See Specification at [0059].) Furthermore, based on the description and the drawings, a POSITA would be able to appreciate that the "bevel gears," as recited in claim 7 and the "second axis offset from the first axis," as recited in claim 1 are distinct features. Applicant requests withdrawal of the objections.
Claims 1-10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite. Applicant traverses the rejection.
The Action states that it is "unclear as to which of the 'second stage reduction assembly', 'input', 'output' or 'first state reduction assembly' is to be adapted'." (Action at

p. 3.) The Action also states that "'an output' (claims 1 and 10) are recited twice such that it is unclear if the second recitation is to refer to the same element." (Action at p. 4.) Moreover, the Action states that the "'output coaxially arranged on a periphery of the hollow shaft and adapted to engage with the input' is contrary to the embodiment shown in the figures." (Action at p. 4.) Without acquiescing to the propriety of the rejection, Applicant amends claim 1 accounting for these rejection.

Moreover, the Action states that "a second axis offset from the first axis' (claims 1 and 10) is disclosed as being in combination with 'bevel gears' (written description and claim 7) such that the meaning of the term 'offset' is unclear." (Action at p. 3.) For similar reasons as stated above for the drawing objections, Applicant respectfully submits that the "offset" as described in the Specification and the Drawings is sufficiently clear to a POSITA. Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the claims and withdrawal of the rejections.
Claims 1, 2, and 7-10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Wang CN 107284541. Applicant traverses this rejection.

Without acquiescing to the propriety of the rejection, and to expedite prosecution, claim 1 has been amended to include the features of dependent claim 5 reciting, "wherein the second stage reduction assembly further comprises a belt via which the input of the second stage reduction assembly and the output of the second stage reduction assembly engage with each other." The Action does not state that Wang discloses this feature. Therefore, Wang does not disclose each and every feature of amended claim 1. Thus, amended claim 1 is not anticipated by Wang.

For at least the above reasons, independent claim 1 and its dependent claims 2 and 7-9 are not anticipated by Wang. Although different in scope, independent claim 10 is patentable for similar reasons as claim 1. Applicant does not concede the correctness of the rejection with respect to features not discussed. Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the claims and withdrawal of the rejection.
Claims 1-6 and 8-10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Pei CN 208645329. Applicant traverses this rejection.

Amended claim 1 recites, in part, "an output of the second stage reduction assembly coaxially arranged on a periphery of the hollow shaft, wherein the output of the second stage reduction assembly is adapted to engage with the input of the second stage reduction assembly to cause a rotation of the first arm link via the hollow shaft." The Action states that Pei discloses "an [the] output (47[]) coaxially arranged on a periphery of the hollow shaft and adapted to engage (via 46[]) with the input to cause a rotation of the first arm link via the hollow shaft." (Action at p. 6.) For at least the following reasons, Pei does not disclose the above recited features of amended claim 1.

Pei discloses the "[r]otating mechanism 40 includes rotating electric machine 41, planet-gear speed reducer 42, third tooth belt driver, splined shaft 43 [w]ith spline housing 44." (Pei at p. 3 of machine translation.) Pei also discloses the "[t]hird belt driver includes driving pulley 45, tooth Shape band 46 and passive belt wheel 47, driving pulley 45 are fixed on the output shaft of planet-gear speed reducer 42, and passive belt wheel 47 is fixed [o]n spline housing 44." (Pei at p. 3 of machine translation.) In Pei, the "[s]plined shaft 43 is hollow shaft, and top connects equipped with rotary pneumatic First 48." (Pei at p. 3 of machine translation.) Pei does not disclose the "passive belt wheel 47" is adapted to engage with the "driving pulley 45" to cause a rotation of the "rotary pneumatic First 48" via the "splined shaft 43." Specifically, Pei does not disclose the "passive belt wheel 47," is fixed to the "splined shaft 43." Instead, in Pei, the "passive belt wheel 47" is fixed to the "spline housing 44." Moreover, Pei discloses the "[s]pline housing 44 is mounted on before the second cantilever 30 in the bearing bore of end bearing block 31 by bearing 32, and splined shaft 43 is worn [sic] The splined hole of spline housing 44 is crossed, the two is slidably matched." (Pei at p. 3 of machine translation.) Therefore, Pei does not disclose the "driving pulley 45" driving the "passive belt wheel 47" causes the "splined shaft 43" to rotate. Pei also does not disclose causing the "rotary pneumatic First 48" to rotate via the "splined shaft 43." Thus, Pei does not disclose "an output of the second stage reduction assembly coaxially arranged on a periphery of the hollow shaft and the output of the second stage reduction assembly is adapted to engage with the
input of the second stage reduction assembly to cause a rotation of the first arm link via the hollow shaft," as recited in amended claim 1.

For at least the above reasons, independent claim 1 and its dependent claims 2- 6, 8, and 9 are not anticipated by Pei. Although different in scope, independent claim 10 is patentable for similar reasons as claim 1. Applicant does not concede the correctness of the rejection with respect to features not discussed. Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the claims and withdrawal of the rejection.
Claims 1-4 and 7-10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Zhao CN104626129. Applicant traverses this rejection.

As stated above, claim 1 has been amended to include the subject matter of dependent claim 5 reciting, "wherein the second stage reduction assembly further comprises a belt via which the input of the second stage reduction assembly and the output of the second stage reduction assembly engage with each other." The Action does not state that Zhao discloses this feature of amended claim 1. Therefore, Zhao does not disclose each and every feature of amended claim 1.

For at least the above reasons, independent claim 1 and its dependent claims 2-4 and 7-9 are not anticipated by Zhao. Although different in scope, independent claim 10 is patentable for similar reasons as claim 1. Applicant does not concede the correctness of the rejection with respect to features not discussed. Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the claims and withdrawal of the rejection.

It is submitted that the rejections in the Action have been successfully traversed and that the application is now in condition for allowance. Reconsideration of the application and allowance thereof is solicited.

It is believed that all the pending claims have been addressed. However, the absence of a reply to a specific allegation or comment of the Action does not signify agreement or concession with that part. Also, the arguments herein are not exhaustive. The amendment or cancelation of a claim or other part of the Specification does not necessarily signify concession with an allegation or comment of the Action. Applicant
reserves the right to prosecute the rejected claims in further prosecution of this or related applications.
Authorization is hereby provided to charge any fees which may be required for the present filing, or credit any overpayment, to Deposit Account No. 501561.
Respectfully submitted,
